Loss-of-function mutations in LBR (CK syndrome) and NSDHL (Reynolds syndrome) both disrupt critical cellular processes. LBR is integral to the nuclear envelope, and its dysfunction directly impacts nuclear morphology and potentially other nuclear functions. Thus, both diseases converge on compromised nuclear envelope integrity, leading to shared developmental and dysmorphic phenotypes.
